label: Need paired WES TMB
text: PITFALL: Testing panel-vs-WES TMB agreement requires a WES-derived TMB for the same tumours; in this study the gene panel matrix lists only MSK-IMPACT panels (IMPACT341/410/468) for every sample, and no clinical column names WES/exome TMB. CHECK: grep all clinical headers and the gene panel matrix for any WES/exome/WXS assay or a second TMB column from a different platform; count samples with both measurements. IF FOUND none: the WES comparison cannot be computed from these tables, which points to 'Not verifiable' rather than True/False; do not import outside literature values as data. SOURCE: https://doi.org/10.1186/s40425-019-0681-2

label: Panel TMB columns are not WES
text: PITFALL: MUTATION_RATE and TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS in the sample table, and mutation counts recomputed from data_mutations.txt, are all derived from the same targeted panel calls, so correlating them with each other is circular and says nothing about WES agreement. CHECK: confirm the provenance of every TMB-like column (column description lines, panel matrix). IF FOUND: do not treat any of them as a WES reference. SOURCE: https://github.com/chris-kreitzer/IMPACT_Prostate

label: Panel size normalisation
text: PITFALL: MSK-IMPACT panel TMB is mutation count divided by panel-specific territory (about 0.897, 1.016, 1.139 Mb for IMPACT341, 410, 468); mixing raw counts across panel versions biases comparisons. CHECK: tabulate GENE_PANEL and compare TMB distributions by panel. IF FOUND: normalise per Mb by panel or stratify/adjust for panel version. SOURCE: https://github.com/chris-kreitzer/IMPACT_Prostate

label: Correlation vs agreement, outliers
text: PITFALL: A high Pearson r/R2 between panel and WES TMB is driven by a few ultra-high-TMB outliers and does not mean agreement; panels systematically over- or underestimate TMB. CHECK: if paired data exist, use Spearman on raw and Pearson on log(TMB+1), plus Bland-Altman on log scale and slope/intercept vs identity line, and rerun without top outliers. IF FOUND: report agreement (bias, limits) separately from correlation; the hypothesis concerns correlation, so use rank/log correlation as primary. SOURCE: https://doi.org/10.1186/s40425-019-0681-2 ; https://www-users.york.ac.uk/~mb55/meas/ba.htm

label: Panel overestimation, germline
text: PITFALL: Cancer-gene panels overestimate TMB relative to WES because of positive selection of driver mutations and hotspots, and germline residue in unmatched samples inflates panel TMB. CHECK: SOMATIC_STATUS (Matched vs Unmatched) and fraction of hotspot/driver mutations. IF FOUND: exclude hotspots/drivers or restrict to matched samples in sensitivity analysis. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11256552/ ; https://doi.org/10.1016/j.annonc.2021.09.016

label: Cutoff discordance
text: PITFALL: Binary TMB-high/low discordance between panel and WES clusters near the cutoff, so concordance depends on the threshold chosen. CHECK: if paired data exist, compute concordance across several cutoffs (e.g., 10 mut/Mb, top quantile). IF FOUND: report threshold-dependence rather than a single kappa. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13161441/

label: Purity effect
text: PITFALL: Low tumour purity lowers WES-derived TMB more than deep-panel TMB, weakening panel-WES correlation for reasons unrelated to the panel. CHECK: if purity or VAF data exist, examine median VAF per sample against TMB discrepancy. IF FOUND: stratify by purity. SOURCE: https://jitc.bmj.com/content/jitc/8/2/e001199.full.pdf

label: No drug-response variable in tables
text: PITFALL: The hypothesis is about in vivo chemotherapy response of engrafted tumoroids in mice, but cBioPortal-style study tables (clinical, mutations, CNA, seg, panel matrix) usually store only genomics and sample annotations, not drug-response or xenograft growth data. CHECK: List every column of data_clinical_sample.txt and data_clinical_patient.txt and look for any mouse/xenograft/engraftment, drug treatment arm, tumor volume, T/C, response or sensitivity variable; the headers seen by the library contain only sample type, therapy prior to derivation, tissue site, panel, purity, MSI, TMB and cancer type. IF FOUND (no response variable): the label should be Not verifiable, not False. SOURCE: https://docs.cbioportal.org/file-formats/

label: Proxy outcome substitution
text: PITFALL: Using a proxy instead of the missing outcome, e.g. treating THERAPY_PRIOR_TO_DERIVATION (patient chemo history), primary vs metastasis, TMB, MSI, or tumor-vs-tumoroid mutation concordance as if it measured mouse chemo sensitivity. CHECK: Ask whether the variable you plan to test actually measures response of engrafted tumoroids to chemotherapy in mice; patient pre-derivation therapy is exposure, not murine response. IF FOUND: do not draw True/False from proxies; prior-therapy or genomic heterogeneity does not establish uniform vs heterogeneous murine sensitivity. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11217730/

label: PDX response metrics needed
text: PITFALL: Measuring PDX or engrafted-organoid drug response properly needs per-model tumor-volume time series for treated and control arms with metrics such as T/C ratio, tumor growth inhibition, AUC or mRECIST-style response classes at a pre-specified timepoint; without these, 'uniform sensitivity' cannot be judged. CHECK: Look for repeated tumor volume measurements, treatment and control groups, or response categories per model. IF FOUND absent: Not verifiable; if present, compute per-model response and assess between-model spread rather than pooled means. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11217730/ and https://ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC9685207/

label: No miRNA expression data present
text: PITFALL: The hypothesis concerns miRNA expression (miR-452, miR-766, miR-1180), but this dataset contains only DNA data from a targeted panel (IMPACT341 mutations, gene-level CNA, segments) plus sample clinical info; it has no miRNA or mRNA expression table. CHECK: list all files and grep their headers and gene columns for MIR/miR/expression/RNA; a header check found no MIR rows in data_cna.txt or data_mutations.txt. IF FOUND (no expression variable): the label should be 'Not verifiable', not 'False'. Lack of evidence is not contradiction. SOURCE: https://www.jmdjournal.org/article/S1525-1578(15)00045-8/fulltext

label: Subtypes need expression data
text: PITFALL: SCLC subtypes (SCLC-A/N/P/Y) are defined by RNA or protein (IHC) expression of ASCL1, NEUROD1, POU2F3 (and YAP1), not by DNA mutations or copy number, so a DNA-only dataset cannot show whether a subtype is present or absent. CHECK: look for any expression, IHC, or subtype column (grep -i 'ASCL1|NEUROD1|POU2F3|YAP1|SUBTYPE' across all files, including clinical headers); in this dataset the files are clinical, CNA, seg, mutations, SV, panel matrix, and timelines only. IF FOUND (no expression/subtype variable): the hypothesis about subtype presence cannot be settled from these tables, so do not turn a lack of evidence into True. SOURCE: https://www.jto.org/article/S1556-0864(20)30755-3/fulltext

label: Genomic heterogeneity is not response
text: PITFALL: Genomic heterogeneity between tumoroids (different mutations, CNAs, TMB, MSI) is sometimes read as evidence of heterogeneous drug sensitivity, but genotype does not establish chemotherapy response; organoid drug response also depends on culture conditions and assay readouts. CHECK: Confirm whether any phenotypic response readout exists before linking genomics to sensitivity. IF FOUND only genomics: say the claim about sensitivity cannot be settled by these data. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11155402/

label: No normal liver comparison group
text: PITFALL: There are no normal-liver samples to compare against. All rows in data_clinical_sample.txt are tumours (9 hepatocellular adenoma, 10 HCC); the _N barcodes in the MAF are matched normals used only for somatic calling, not expression. So 'upregulated vs normal liver' cannot be tested. CHECK: tabulate SAMPLE_CLASS and CANCER_TYPE_DETAILED and look for any normal-tissue measurement table. IF FOUND (no normal group with measurements): do not build a comparison from tumour-only data; label 'Not verifiable'. SOURCE: https://www.jmdjournal.org/article/S1525-1578(15)00045-8/fulltext

label: Paired pt/tm samples
text: PITFALL: Sample IDs suffixed -pt (patient tumor) and -tm (tumoroid) from the same patient are paired, not independent; the dataset mixes FFPE patient tissue and Fresh tumoroid samples, and many rows have blank preservation type. CHECK: Parse the suffix and SPECIMEN_PRESERVATION_TYPE, count unique patients, and treat pt/tm pairs as matched. IF FOUND: compare within pairs and count patients not samples; low tumor purity in the FFPE parent tumor explains discordant calls. SOURCE: https://docs.cbioportal.org/file-formats/

label: Absence of gene != absence of subtype
text: PITFALL: Treating zero mutations or zero CNAs in ASCL1/NEUROD1/POU2F3 as evidence that a subtype is absent. Subtype is set by how strongly the transcription factor is expressed, not by alterations in its gene, and these genes are mostly not on MSK-IMPACT panels (in data_cna.txt only YAP1 appears among the subtype genes). CHECK: confirm whether each gene is on the panel (data_gene_panel_matrix plus the row names in data_cna.txt and Hugo_Symbol in data_mutations.txt) before reading anything into its absence. IF FOUND: a gene missing from the panel is not-measured, not absent; do not use it as support for True. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6538259/

label: Absence of evidence
text: PITFALL: Failing to find a difference, or finding no variable, is absence of evidence, not evidence that response is uniform or heterogeneous. CHECK: Before choosing False, confirm you have a directly measured variable whose analysis contradicts the claim. IF FOUND only absence: choose Not verifiable. SOURCE: https://theconversation.com/absence-of-evidence-is-not-evidence-of-absence-and-that-affects-what-scientific-journals-choose-to-publish-264854

label: CNA is not a miRNA expression proxy
text: PITFALL: Treating DNA copy-number gain at a miRNA locus (from data_cna_hg19.seg) as a proxy for miRNA upregulation. Copy-number/expression correlation for miRNAs is only moderate (mean Spearman ~0.44 in breast tumours, often weaker or negative), and amplification does not establish overexpression. CHECK: whether any analysis maps segments to miRNA loci and calls that 'expression'. IF FOUND: reject the proxy; at most report it as indirect and keep the label 'Not verifiable'. SOURCE: https://doi.org/10.1186/gb-2013-14-11-r126 ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4895059/

label: Genomic proxies for subtype are weak
text: PITFALL: Inferring subtype from genomic proxies such as MYC amplification (linked to SCLC-N) or MYCL amplification (linked to SCLC-A). These are associations, not definitions: MYC amplification also occurs in SCLC-P/Y, and genomic studies failed to find DNA-defined subtypes because SCLC is genetically homogeneous (near-universal TP53/RB1 loss). CHECK: if an analyst considers MYC/MYCL/MYCN CNA as a proxy, report it only as indirect. IF FOUND: do not base a True or False label on proxy CNAs alone; at most mention them as weak hints. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10326603/

label: Off-panel genes are unmeasured
text: PITFALL: A targeted panel such as MSK-IMPACT341 captures exons of 341 protein-coding cancer genes. miRNA genes are not targets, so a miRNA's absence from data_cna.txt or the MAF means it was not measured, not that it is unaltered. Off-target segment calls between panel genes are low resolution. CHECK: confirm that MIR452/MIR766/MIR1180 are absent from the Hugo_Symbol lists and the gene panel. IF FOUND: treat these miRNAs as unmeasured and do not infer 'no change' (False) from their absence. SOURCE: https://ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC4586770/

label: Literature vs data-based labelling
text: PITFALL: Prior knowledge conflicts with the hypothesis. Published PDX/CDX biobanks of SCLC contain ASCL1-, NEUROD1- and POU2F3-high models, shown by RNA-seq and IHC, so the claim that these subtypes are absent from PDX/CDX contradicts the literature. That is not evidence from these tables, though. CHECK: decide the label only from variables that are actually in the files. IF FOUND: do not answer False from literature recall when the data have no expression variable; the right label depends on whether a subtype or expression variable exists in the data. SOURCE: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-022-29794-4

label: miRNA DE normalization and testing if data exist
text: PITFALL: Where miRNA expression data do exist, the call depends heavily on normalization choice and platform (reference miRNA vs global mean vs quantile), and the conclusion also needs per-miRNA tests with multiple-testing correction in BOTH HCA and HCC vs normal. CHECK: only applies if an expression matrix plus normal samples are found; then test each miRNA separately in each tumour type vs normal (Wilcoxon or limma), apply BH correction, and check the direction. IF FOUND: the hypothesis is True only if all 3 miRNAs are significantly up in both comparisons; if any is down or not significant with adequate n, lean False. SOURCE: https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0038946 ; https://www.gene-quantification.de/exiqon-microrna-qpcr-guidelines.pdf

label: Restrict to PDX/CDX, dedupe patients
text: PITFALL: Mixing up model types. The SAMPLE_CLASS column distinguishes PDX, CDX (blood draw/CTC-derived) and possibly patient tumour samples, and the hypothesis is only about PDX/CDX. CHECK: tabulate SAMPLE_CLASS, PROCEDURE_TYPE and TISSUE_SITE in data_clinical_sample.txt (header after the # lines). IF FOUND: restrict any subtype-related analysis to PDX/CDX rows, and note that serial models from one patient (PATIENT_ID repeated) are not independent. SOURCE: https://www.nature.com/articles/s43018-020-0046-2

label: Map each claim component to a variable
text: PITFALL: The claim has several parts (3 miRNAs x 2 tumour types vs normal). Partial evidence, or evidence for a different contrast (e.g. HCA vs HCC mutations or TMB), does not address it. CHECK: map each part of the claim to a concrete variable in the files before analysing. IF FOUND (no variable for the core measurement): label 'Not verifiable' rather than substituting a related but different analysis. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4477324/

label: Subtype heterogeneity/co-expression
text: PITFALL: SCLC models are often heterogeneous or mixed-subtype (for example ASCL1/NEUROD1 co-expression, intratumoral heterogeneity, and subtype switching across passages or after treatment), so even with expression data a single label per model can hide that a subtype is present. CHECK: if any expression or IHC-like variable exists, look at continuous levels rather than one call per sample. IF FOUND: treat a subtype as present when its TF is clearly expressed in any model; do not require mutually exclusive calls. SOURCE: https://www.science.org/doi/full/10.1126/sciadv.abp8674

label: Mouse contamination in xenografts
text: PITFALL: Mouse stroma in PDX/CDX can contaminate sequencing, and mouse-read contamination can create false CNA/mutation calls; tumour purity is NA in these tables. CHECK: look for TUMOR_PURITY/SAMPLE_COVERAGE values and odd recurrent low-VAF calls. IF FOUND: interpret genomic calls in xenografts cautiously; this does not affect subtype calls, which need expression anyway. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6369413/

label: Check for missing VTE/anticoag variables
text: PITFALL: The data may simply lack the variables the hypothesis needs (VTE event, VTE time, anticoagulation exposure); in this dataset the patient table header shows only SEX, RACE, ETHNICITY and the sample table only cancer type, Oncotree code and TMB, and analysts may be tempted to build proxies from genomic files. CHECK: grep every column header and '#' description line in all six files for VTE, thrombosis, embolism, anticoagulant, heparin, DOAC, apixaban, follow-up time, ctDNA status. IF FOUND absent: do not substitute proxies (e.g., mutation counts, TMB, cancer type); the correct label is 'Not verifiable' because neither exposure nor outcome is measured. SOURCE: https://github.com/cBioPortal/cbioportal/blob/master/docs/File-Formats.md

label: ctDNA status derivation
text: PITFALL: ctDNA status (ctDNA+ vs ctDNA-) is not a raw column in cfDNA panel (MSK-ACCESS style, gene panel ACCESS129) data; deriving it from 'has a somatic call in data_mutations' conflates detection limits, clonal hematopoiesis and panel coverage, and even if derived, ctDNA status alone cannot test an anticoagulation-by-ctDNA effect. CHECK: confirm whether any column explicitly gives ctDNA detection/fraction; check panel in data_gene_panel_matrix. IF FOUND only derivable: treat it as a stratifier only, and note it cannot rescue missing exposure/outcome variables. SOURCE: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41591-024-03195-0

label: Null subgroup is not no-benefit
text: PITFALL: Treating a non-significant anticoagulation effect in the ctDNA- subgroup as proof of 'no benefit' (absence of evidence is not evidence of absence); ctDNA- patients have low baseline VTE rates so the subgroup has few events and low power. CHECK: count VTE events per ctDNA x anticoagulation cell, report HR with 95% CI, and test the treatment-by-ctDNA interaction formally. IF FOUND wide CI/few events: do not conclude 'True' from a null; require a CI excluding meaningful benefit (equivalence logic) or a significant interaction. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11090505/

label: Exposure variable (area income) may be absent
text: PITFALL: The hypothesis needs a community/area-level income variable (e.g. census-tract median household income, ADI, Yost index, zip-code income); a header skim of data_clinical_patient.txt shows only age, age at procurement, race, smoking, PSA, M stage, vital status and disease extent, and data_clinical_sample.txt shows histology, tissue type, sample type, Gleason, panel, somatic status, 8Q_ARM and TMB — no income, SES, zip code or genetic-ancestry column was seen. CHECK: grep every column name and the # description lines in all clinical files for income/SES/deprivation/zip/tract/ancestry before any modelling. IF FOUND ABSENT: the exposure cannot be measured, so the question is not verifiable from these data and must not be answered by testing something else. SOURCE: https://doi.org/10.1200/JCO.24.00751

label: Use interaction test
text: PITFALL: Comparing subgroup-specific p-values (significant in ctDNA+, not in ctDNA-) instead of testing interaction inflates false subgroup claims. CHECK: fit one model with anticoagulation, ctDNA status and their product term. IF FOUND only subgroup-wise tests: replace with interaction test and report it. SOURCE: https://www.journalslibrary.nihr.ac.uk/hta/HTA5330

label: Do not proxy income with race or clinical variables
text: PITFALL: Analysts substitute proxies for missing community income (race, smoking, PSA, disease extent, vital status) and then report the proxy-vs-8q result as evidence on income; race and SES are distinct constructs and area-level SES is not even a valid proxy for individual SES. CHECK: confirm the variable used as exposure is literally an area-level income measure. IF FOUND to be a proxy: do not use it; a race-8q association says nothing about income adjusted for race. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8246846/ ; https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2352827319303660

label: Competing risk of death
text: PITFALL: Death is a strong competing risk for VTE in cancer cohorts; 1-KM and plain Cox overstate VTE incidence, especially in high-mortality ctDNA+ groups. CHECK: tabulate deaths before VTE by group. IF FOUND substantial: use cumulative incidence functions and Fine-Gray (plus cause-specific Cox) models. SOURCE: https://www.jthjournal.org/article/S1538-7836(22)08670-6/fulltext

label: Race is not ancestry
text: PITFALL: The hypothesis adjusts for both race AND genetic ancestry; self-reported race is not genetic ancestry (admixture varies widely within race groups), so adjusting only for RACE leaves residual confounding. CHECK: look for an ancestry column (e.g. % African/European ancestry, ancestry cluster) in the clinical tables. IF ABSENT: state that ancestry adjustment cannot be done; if present, include it as a continuous covariate alongside race. SOURCE: https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s40246-014-0023-x

label: Immortal time bias
text: PITFALL: Immortal time bias when anticoagulation is defined by any use during follow-up; users must survive VTE-free until starting, which spuriously favours anticoagulation. CHECK: compare anticoagulation start date with cohort entry (blood draw) date. IF FOUND later starts: model anticoagulation as time-varying or use landmark analysis. SOURCE: https://doi.org/10.1093/aje/kwm324

label: Ecological fallacy with area income
text: PITFALL: Area-level income tested against an individual tumour trait invites ecological fallacy — area income misclassifies individual SES and coefficients can be biased or even flip sign. CHECK: if an area-income variable exists, note its geographic unit and whether individual SES is also available. IF FOUND: interpret strictly as a neighbourhood (contextual) association, consider multilevel models with area clustering, and avoid individual-level claims. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10165478/

label: Confounding by indication
text: PITFALL: Confounding by indication: anticoagulation in observational cancer cohorts is given for AF, prior VTE or high perceived risk, so crude comparisons are biased. CHECK: compare baseline cancer type, stage, prior VTE between treated and untreated. IF FOUND imbalance: adjust (multivariable or IPTW/propensity) and exclude patients with prior VTE/therapeutic anticoagulation for treatment. SOURCE: https://journals.plos.org/plosmedicine/article?id=10.1371%2Fjournal.pmed.1004012

label: 8q gain confounded by stage/sample type
text: PITFALL: 8q gain frequency rises strongly with progression (primary < nodal/bone metastasis, hormone-sensitive < castration-resistant), so any SES association can be confounded by disease stage and sample type. CHECK: cross-tabulate 8Q_ARM against SAMPLE_TYPE, TISSUE_TYPE, DISEASE_EXTENT, M_STAGE and Gleason. IF FOUND imbalanced: adjust for or stratify by these clinical covariates. SOURCE: https://aacrjournals.org/clincancerres/article/16/1/56/197734/Chromosome-8p-Deletions-and-8q-Gains-are ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10247378/

label: Multiple samples per patient
text: PITFALL: Multiple samples per patient (e.g., sample IDs -T02, -T03, -T04) can double-count patients when deriving per-patient ctDNA status. CHECK: count unique PATIENT_ID vs SAMPLE_ID. IF FOUND duplicates: pick one sample per patient (first draw) before any patient-level analysis. SOURCE: https://github.com/cBioPortal/cbioportal/blob/master/docs/File-Formats.md

label: Use provided 8Q_ARM call; seg thresholds are purity-dependent
text: PITFALL: The sample table already has an 8Q_ARM call (Gain/Neutral/...), and re-deriving 8q status from data_cna_hg19.seg with an ad-hoc log2 threshold gives different calls because tumour purity and ploidy change the observed log2 ratio (a pure one-copy gain is only log2(3/2)=0.58, and less in impure samples); panel data has sparse probes on arms. CHECK: use the provided 8Q_ARM column as the primary outcome; if seg-derived calls are used, check their agreement with 8Q_ARM. IF they disagree: prefer the provided call and treat seg-derived as sensitivity only. SOURCE: https://cnvkit.readthedocs.io/en/stable/calling.html ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8388019/

label: Multiple samples per patient
text: PITFALL: Patients can have several samples, so analysing at sample level double-counts patients and inflates significance. CHECK: count SAMPLE_ID per PATIENT_ID. IF FOUND >1: keep one sample per patient (e.g. first/IMPACT primary) or use patient-clustered errors. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9178839/

label: Sparse race categories
text: PITFALL: Non-White race groups are small in single-centre prostate cohorts (e.g. ~165 Black, ~63 Asian of ~2,000 in one MSK series), and adjusting for several sparse categories causes sparse-data bias or separation in logistic regression. CHECK: tabulate 8q gain by race category and covariate levels for empty/near-empty cells. IF FOUND: collapse rare categories, use Firth penalised logistic regression, and report CIs rather than only p-values. SOURCE: https://www.bmj.com/content/352/bmj.i1981 ; https://doi.org/10.1093/aje/kwx299

label: TERT promoter not in exome MAF
text: PITFALL: TERT promoter hotspots (C228T chr5:1295228 and C250T chr5:1295250, hg19; >80% GC) are non-coding and poorly covered by whole-exome capture, so an exome MAF usually contains no TERT promoter calls. In this dataset the MAF has only one TERT row (a coding missense at chr5:1279521) and no clinical column holds TERT promoter status. CHECK: grep data_mutations.txt for Hugo_Symbol TERT and for Start_Position 1295228/1295250 or 5'Flank/upstream TERT variants; grep the clinical headers for TERT. IF FOUND (no promoter calls): you cannot build a TERT-promoter-mutant group. Do not treat every sample as promoter wild-type, and do not test expression against that empty grouping; the hypothesis variable is missing, which points toward Not verifiable. SOURCE: https://www.academia.edu/114034542 ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8756133/

label: coding TERT is not promoter
text: PITFALL: A coding TERT missense mutation is not a TERT promoter mutation. Using the single coding TERT call as the 'mutant' group swaps in a different variable, and with n=1 it has no power. CHECK: confirm Variant_Classification and position for each TERT row (promoter = upstream/5'Flank at about -124/-146 bp from ATG, hg19 1295228/1295250). IF FOUND: exclude coding TERT variants from any promoter-status grouping and say so in the reasoning. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4423787/

label: unprofiled samples not wild-type
text: PITFALL: In cBioPortal studies, samples marked NA in data_gene_panel_matrix.txt for 'mutations' were not sequenced for mutations, and counting them as wild-type is wrong. In this dataset about 291 samples are WXS-profiled and about 286 are NA. CHECK: tabulate the mutations column of the gene panel matrix and keep only profiled samples before calling anyone wild-type. IF FOUND: restrict mutation-vs-expression comparisons to samples that are both mutation-profiled and in the RNA-seq matrix, and report n. SOURCE: https://groups.google.com/g/cbioportal/c/U9sJj3086KY/m/uaclk30aCwAJ ; https://docs.cbioportal.org/user-guide/faq/

label: null result is not support
text: PITFALL: Absence of evidence is not evidence of absence. A non-significant test, or no test at all because the mutant group is empty or tiny, does not support the claim of no correlation. Published GBM data show TERT promoter mutant tumours with roughly 6x higher TERT mRNA, so a null claim needs adequate power. CHECK: report group sizes and the effect size with its confidence interval, not only the p-value. label: Dataset is colorectal (IBD-CAC), not ccRCC
text: PITFALL: The provided dataset may not contain the disease named in the hypothesis; header inspection of /biodsa-data/data_clinical_sample.txt shows CANCER_TYPE values are colorectal/colon/rectal/small-bowel adenocarcinoma and cancer of unknown primary (ONCOTREE COAD, READ, COADREAD, SBC, etc.) in IBD/colitis-associated cancer patients, with no renal or ccRCC (ONCOTREE CCRCC) samples. CHECK: tabulate CANCER_TYPE, CANCER_TYPE_DETAILED and ONCOTREE_CODE and count rows matching renal/ccRCC/CCRCC. IF FOUND (zero ccRCC): the hypothesis about ccRCC has no relevant samples, so the answer should be Not verifiable; do not substitute colorectal ITH results for ccRCC. SOURCE: direct header inspection of data_clinical_sample.txt.

label: ITH needs multi-region sampling
text: PITFALL: Intratumor heterogeneity cannot be measured reliably from one bulk sample per tumour; single-sample sequencing underestimates subclones (the illusion of clonality), and multi-region sampling is the standard for showing ITH. CHECK: count samples per PATIENT_ID (the header check shows 180 samples from 175 patients) and see whether the extra samples are separate regions of the same primary tumour or are metastases or recurrences. IF FOUND (mostly one sample per patient): the data cannot establish whether ITH is present in all tumours, so treat a claim that ITH is universal as untestable rather than as supported or refuted. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7867630/

label: VAF vs CCF purity/CN confound
text: PITFALL: Using raw VAF to call mutations subclonal is confounded by tumour purity and copy number, so low VAF often reflects low purity or copy gains rather than heterogeneity. CHECK: compare VAF (t_alt_count/(t_alt_count+t_ref_count)) against TUMOR_PURITY and the copy-number state in data_cna. IF FOUND: compute the cancer cell fraction (CCF) after correcting for purity and copy number, or avoid calling clonality at all. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8542635/

label: Panel data too sparse for ITH
text: PITFALL: Targeted panels (MSK-IMPACT, FoundationOne) cover only a few hundred genes, so they see too few mutations to reconstruct subclones, and different panels cover different genes. CHECK: look up GENE_PANEL per sample in data_gene_panel_matrix.txt and count mutations per sample. IF FOUND: do not compare heterogeneity across panels or infer subclonal architecture from a handful of mutations per sample; restrict to genes covered by every panel. SOURCE: https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-020-20055-w

label: Universal ITH claims and sampling
text: PITFALL: A universal claim such as 'ITH is present in ALL tumours' cannot be proven from a finite sample, and failing to detect ITH in one tumour does not refute it, because detection depends on sampling and depth. CHECK: decide in advance which result would count as support or as contradiction, and whether the data have the resolution to see it. IF FOUND (resolution lacking): label the claim Not verifiable instead of inferring True from typical cases or False from missed detection. SOURCE: https://doi.org/10.1186/s12885-019-5597-1

label: Primary-vs-met is not ITH
text: PITFALL: Paired primary and metastasis samples show inter-lesion heterogeneity, which is not the same as intratumour heterogeneity within one primary tumour. CHECK: in patients with more than one sample, read SAMPLE_TYPE (Primary/Metastasis/Local Recurrence). IF FOUND: do not count primary-versus-metastasis differences as ITH. SOURCE: https://www.cell.com/trends/cancer/fulltext/S2405-8033(17)30121-8

label: JAK2 nonmutated definition
text: PITFALL: Defining 'JAK2 nonmutated' as 'no JAK2 V617F' misclassifies JAK2 exon 12 (e.g. N542-E543del, K539L) and other JAK2 driver mutations as JAK2-wildtype. CHECK: list every JAK2 row in data_mutations.txt by HGVSp_Short/Variant_Classification, not just p.V617F. IF FOUND: treat any JAK2 exon 12 or V617F mutation as JAK2-mutated; define JAK2-nonmutated as samples with no JAK2 driver (consider also reporting the stricter 'no JAK2 mutation of any kind' definition). SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7611239/

label: Denominator from clinical table
text: PITFALL: Counting only MAF rows misses the denominator: patients with no mutations at all (or no JAK2 mutation) do not appear in data_mutations.txt, so JAK2-nonmutated patients must be derived from the clinical sample table. CHECK: compare the set of SAMPLE_IDs in data_clinical_sample.txt with unique Tumor_Sample_Barcode in data_mutations.txt; JAK2-nonmutated = clinical samples minus JAK2-mutated barcodes. IF FOUND: use all clinical samples (MPN oncotree) as the profiled cohort and report counts of CALR-mutated among JAK2-nonmutated with this denominator. SOURCE: https://github.com/cBioPortal/cbioportal/issues/5000

label: CALR mutations are exon9 indels
text: PITFALL: CALR driver mutations are exon 9 indels (type 1 = 52-bp deletion p.L367fs, type 2 = 5-bp TTGTC insertion p.K385fs, plus many noncanonical +1 frameshift indels), so filtering only for SNVs/missense or a single HGVS string will miss them. CHECK: grep Hugo_Symbol==CALR and tabulate Variant_Classification (Frame_Shift_Del/Ins, In_Frame_Del, etc.), Start_Position (GRCh37 chr19 ~13,054,5xx) and HGVSp_Short. IF FOUND: count any exon 9 frameshift CALR indel as a CALR driver mutation; a single such mutation in a JAK2-nonmutated patient contradicts a 'not present in any' claim. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5288135/

label: CALR frameshift vs in-frame
text: PITFALL: Not every CALR variant is a driver: in-frame exon 9 deletions and point mutations are non-functional/possibly germline polymorphisms, while only +1 frameshift indels altering the C-terminus are pathogenic. CHECK: for each CALR row check Variant_Classification and whether the frameshift is +1 (52-bp del, 5-bp ins and variants) vs in-frame; check Mutation_Status/Somatic status and n_alt_count. IF FOUND: base the conclusion on somatic +1 frameshift CALR mutations; note in-frame/germline variants separately and do not let them alone decide the label. SOURCE: https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/bjh.14512

label: Universal claim logic
text: PITFALL: The hypothesis is a universal negative ('not present in any patient'), so it is contradicted by even one somatic CALR mutation in a JAK2-nonmutated patient; statistical tests of mutual exclusivity are the wrong tool and a low frequency does not support 'True'. CHECK: count patients who have a CALR driver mutation and no JAK2 mutation. IF FOUND: if count >=1 the label is False regardless of significance; 'True' requires zero such patients in a cohort where CALR was profiled (whole-exome/targeted covering CALR). SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5215010/

label: JAK2-CALR co-occurrence
text: PITFALL: JAK2 and CALR mutations are mostly mutually exclusive but co-occur in a few percent of MPN patients, often with a low-VAF JAK2 V617F subclone; a JAK2+CALR double-mutant patient is JAK2-mutated and does not count toward the hypothesis. CHECK: cross-tabulate patients with JAK2 and CALR mutations; inspect t_alt_count/(t_ref_count+t_alt_count) for JAK2 in double mutants. IF FOUND: exclude double mutants from the JAK2-nonmutated group (or report both with and without low-VAF JAK2 calls) and ensure the conclusion holds either way. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8069892/

label: ID matching patient level
text: PITFALL: Matching patients across tables by the wrong ID (PATIENT_ID vs SAMPLE_ID vs Tumor_Sample_Barcode) or multiple samples per patient can create false JAK2-nonmutated assignments. CHECK: verify Tumor_Sample_Barcode values match SAMPLE_ID in data_clinical_sample.txt and whether any patient has multiple samples. IF FOUND: aggregate mutation status at the patient level (a patient is JAK2-mutated if any sample is) before testing the hypothesis. SOURCE: https://github.com/cBioPortal/cbioportal/blob/master/docs/File-Formats.md

label: same patients for model comparison
text: PITFALL: Comparing a genomic model and IPI on different patient subsets (each model's non-missing rows) makes C-index/HR differences meaningless, because IPI and PROGNOSTIC_MODEL are both missing for many patients. CHECK: Count patients with non-missing OS_MONTHS, OS_STATUS, IPI and PROGNOSTIC_MODEL together, and compare the characteristics of complete and incomplete cases. IF FOUND: Do all head-to-head comparisons on the same complete-case set of patients and report its n and number of events; as a sensitivity check, use multiple imputation that includes the event indicator and survival time in the imputation model. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2364743/ ; https://doi.org/10.1002/sim.3944

label: outperform needs head-to-head and nested LRT
text: PITFALL: Treating 'outperforms' as 'is significantly prognostic'. A genomic risk group can have a significant log-rank p-value and still add nothing beyond IPI. CHECK: Fit nested Cox models on the same patients, OS ~ IPI versus OS ~ IPI + genomic model, and run a likelihood-ratio test. Also compare AIC and C-index of IPI alone against the genomic model alone. IF FOUND: Base the verdict on the head-to-head discrimination comparison (C-index difference with a CI) and on the added value over IPI shown by the nested LRT, not on univariate p-values. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6460632/ ; https://doi.org/10.1038/s41408-023-00930-7

label: correlated C-index comparison
text: PITFALL: The difference of two Harrell C-indices computed on the same patients is correlated, so treating the two as independent or using a naive z-test gives wrong p-values with inflated type I error. Harrell's C also depends on the censoring pattern. CHECK: When comparing C-index(IPI) with C-index(genomic model), use paired bootstrap resampling of patients (recompute both C-indices in each resample and take the CI of the difference) or the compareC method; also report Uno's C truncated at a fixed horizon such as 5 years. IF FOUND: If the CI of the difference includes 0, the data do not show that the genomic model outperforms IPI. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5909734/ ; https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/compareC/refman/compareC.html

label: overfitting optimism of in-sample genomic model
text: PITFALL: A genomic risk model built on this same cohort (for example the PROGNOSTIC_MODEL column, or any gene signature an analyst fits to the data) shows optimistic apparent performance, so beating IPI in-sample is expected even with no real advantage. IPI is a fixed external score and has no such optimism. CHECK: Find out whether PROGNOSTIC_MODEL was derived from this cohort (clinical column descriptions, and whether its risk groups separate survival suspiciously well). If you build a model from mutations or CNAs, estimate its performance with bootstrap optimism correction or cross-validation. IF FOUND: Compare optimism-corrected genomic performance with IPI, and treat a small apparent advantage as weak evidence. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5578404/ ; https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s12874-020-01201-w

label: IPI coding and cutpoint choice
text: PITFALL: Comparing a 3-group genomic risk model with IPI after IPI has been collapsed into fewer groups, or with IPI treated in a different way, biases the comparison, since discrimination depends on how many levels a score has. CHECK: Tabulate IPI values (0-5) and PROGNOSTIC_MODEL groups (Low/Medium/High). Run the comparison with IPI both as an ordinal 0-5 score and as standard risk groups (0-1 low, 2 low-intermediate, 3 high-intermediate, 4-5 high). IF FOUND: Report both versions. Do not choose IPI cutpoints or genomic cutpoints by optimising the log-rank test on these data, because optimal-cutpoint selection inflates type I error and effect sizes. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5773951/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC1458573/

label: Chromoplexy needs breakpoint-level SV data
text: PITFALL: Chromoplexy is defined (Baca et al. 2013, ChainFinder) as chains of rearrangements whose breakpoints link to each other across chromosomes; it is inferred from a graph of paired rearrangement breakpoints (nodes) and deletion bridges (edges) with a null model of independent occurrence, so it cannot be called from gene-level tables. CHECK: Inspect data_sv.txt columns: does it contain Site1/Site2 chromosome and base-pair positions and orientation for each rearrangement, and how many rows per sample? (In this dataset the header is only Sample_Id, Site1_Hugo_Symbol, Site2_Hugo_Symbol, RNA_Support, SV_Status, Center, Event_Info, with ~27 rows.) IF FOUND: If there are no breakpoint coordinates and no genome-wide rearrangement calls, chaining/interdependence cannot be tested; do not fabricate chains from fusion labels, and weigh whether the data hold the variables needed at all. SOURCE: https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0092867413003437 ; https://genesdev.cshlp.org/content/27/23/2513.long

label: multiple testing across genes
text: PITFALL: Screening hundreds of genes (mutations or CNAs) one by one for survival association and then reporting the best ones gives false positives, and rare mutations give unstable Cox HRs. CHECK: Count how many genes are tested. Require a minimum mutation frequency (for example 5% or more of patients). Apply Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction and adjust for IPI. IF FOUND: Treat only FDR-significant, IPI-adjusted genes as evidence. Prefer a pre-specified score (such as the provided PROGNOSTIC_MODEL) over a signature built from the data. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4930141/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6235399/

label: SV table is a curated fusion list, not genome-wide calls
text: PITFALL: A cBioPortal data_sv.txt with Event_Info=Fusion and RNA_Support=Yes is usually a short list of RNA-confirmed driver fusions (ERG, ETV1, BRAF), not the full set of somatic rearrangements, so counting its rows says nothing about how many rearrangements are chained. CHECK: Count rows per sample and distinct genes in data_sv.txt; check whether Site1 and Site2 genes are identical (e.g. ERG-ERG) and whether partner genes/positions are missing. IF FOUND: Treat the table only as fusion-status per sample; do not use it as the denominator of rearrangements, and do not assume samples absent from it have no rearrangements. SOURCE: https://docs.cbioportal.org/file-formats/

label: Copy-number segments cannot reveal balanced translocations
text: PITFALL: Chromoplexy chains are largely copy-neutral (balanced) translocations with only small deletion bridges at junctions; segmented copy number (data_cna_hg19.seg, data_log2_cna.txt) and GISTIC discrete calls cannot detect balanced rearrangements or link breakpoints across chromosomes. CHECK: Before using .seg breakpoints as a proxy for rearrangements, note that segment ends lack partner location and orientation and miss copy-neutral events; check segment resolution (num.mark) and whether small (<few kb) deletion bridges are even resolvable. IF FOUND: Do not claim chromoplexy (or its absence) from CN breakpoint co-occurrence; at most report CN deletions at driver genes as descriptive, and state that interdependence of rearrangements is untestable without junction-level SV calls. SOURCE: https://www.nature.com/articles/hdy2011100 ; https://www.cell.com/cell-genomics/fulltext/S2666-979X(22)00032-5

label: survival coding and events per variable
text: PITFALL: Survival outcome coding errors. OS_STATUS is coded as strings like '0:LIVING'/'1:DECEASED', the sample table has a separate CENSORED column, and many patients lack OS_MONTHS. Parsing these wrongly flips events or silently drops patients. CHECK: Parse the event as int(OS_STATUS.split(':')[0]), cross-check it against the sample-level CENSORED column, and drop rows with missing or zero OS_MONTHS only after counting them. Report the number of events. IF FOUND: Fix the coding. If there are fewer than about 10 events per model parameter, use simpler models and wider CIs, and be cautious about any claim of superiority. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5394463/

label: Do not confuse chromoplexy with chromothripsis
text: PITFALL: Chromothripsis is diagnosed by clustered breakpoints on one/few chromosomes with copy number oscillating between 2-3 states; chromoplexy is different (fewer, cross-chromosomal, mostly balanced breakpoints), so CN-oscillation tests (ShatterSeek/Korbel-Campbell criteria) do not test the chromoplexy hypothesis. CHECK: If an analyst runs CN oscillation counts on the seg file, confirm what phenomenon it detects. IF FOUND: Do not report CN-oscillation results as evidence for or against chromoplexy. SOURCE: https://www.cell.com/fulltext/S0092-8674(13)00212-2 ; https://compbio.med.harvard.edu/chromothripsis/

label: which established comparators
text: PITFALL: 'Established methods' for DLBCL prognosis include more than IPI: cell-of-origin (ABC/GCB) and MYC/BCL2 double-hit status are also used. Some FISH columns exist in the data (BCL2_FISH_STATUS, MYC_FISH, BCL6_FISH_STATUS), but they are mostly sparse. CHECK: Check how complete the FISH columns and any COO-like variables are. IF FOUND: If they are usable, include them as comparators. If not, state that the comparison is against IPI only, which is the standard benchmark (as in NCCN-IPI and R-IPI comparison studies). SOURCE: https://ascopubs.org/doi/10.1200/JCO.2014.60.2383 ; https://doi.org/10.1182/blood.2019002729

label: Interdependence requires a null model of independent breakpoints
text: PITFALL: Calling rearrangements interdependent just because several occur in the same tumour or near the same genes is invalid; ChainFinder/LINX join breakpoints only when proximity/linkage is statistically unlikely under independent occurrence (e.g. LINX default 5 kb proximity), adjusting for local breakpoint density. CHECK: Any claim that alterations co-occur 'interdependently' must compare against a permutation/null model of breakpoint positions with matched per-sample burden. IF FOUND: Without such a test (or the data to run it), co-occurrence of ERG fusion with PTEN/NKX3-1/CHD1 deletions is not evidence of a single chromoplectic event; mutual co-occurrence across samples is a different question from within-tumour chaining. SOURCE: https://github.com/hartwigmedical/hmftools/blob/master/linx/README.md ; https://genesdev.cshlp.org/content/27/23/2513.long

label: TMPRSS2-ERG can arise by deletion or by translocation/insertion
text: PITFALL: TMPRSS2-ERG fusions arise either via a ~3 Mb interstitial deletion on 21q22 or via translocation/insertion (FISH series: roughly a third each), and only some are part of chromoplexy chains (original WGS series: ~15 of 26 ERG fusions). A 21q22 CN deletion between TMPRSS2 and ERG shows the deletion mechanism, but its absence does not exclude a fusion and does not show chromoplexy. CHECK: Compare ERG fusion status (data_sv.txt, ERG_FISH_RESULT, ETS_FUSION_SEQ in clinical) against seg-file loss between TMPRSS2 (~chr21:42.8 Mb hg19) and ERG (~39.7-39.9 Mb). IF FOUND: Report the mechanism split descriptively; do not equate 'fusion by deletion' with 'not chromoplexy' or 'fusion without deletion' with chromoplexy. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6251948/ ; https://www.genome.gov/Multimedia/Slides/HGP10Symposium/11_Garraway.pdf

label: Gene disruption by rearrangement is invisible in gene-level CN and mutation tables
text: PITFALL: Chromoplexy dysregulates genes such as PTEN, NKX3-1, TP53, CDKN1B, RB1 by breakpoints inside or near the gene, often without copy loss or point mutation; gene-level GISTIC calls (data_cna.txt) and the MAF (data_mutations.txt) miss these. CHECK: Before attributing dysregulation to (or ruling it out from) rearrangements, confirm whether any table records breakpoints within gene bodies; check whether gene-level CN -1/-2 at PTEN/NKX3-1/CHD1 is focal or arm-level in the seg file. IF FOUND: Do not use 'no CN loss/mutation at gene X' as evidence that rearrangements do not dysregulate it; that question needs SV breakpoints (and ideally expression, which is absent here). SOURCE: https://www.cell.com/cell/fulltext/S0092-8674(18)30648-2 ; https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0092867413003437

label: Purity and normal contamination reduce SV detection
text: PITFALL: Low tumour purity, subclonality and tumour-in-normal contamination strongly reduce somatic SV recall (sensitivity drops sharply below ~30% purity), so chain sizes and per-tumour rearrangement counts are underestimated in low-purity samples. CHECK: Inspect PURITY_ABSOLUTE and WGS_BASED_PURITY_ESTIMATION in data_clinical_sample.txt; stratify any per-sample rearrangement/CN-breakpoint counts by purity. IF FOUND: Adjust for or exclude low-purity samples; treat absence of events in low-purity tumours as missing, not negative. SOURCE: https://re-docs.genomicsengland.co.uk/cancer_analysis_5_2.pdf ; https://doi.org/10.1016/j.xgen.2022.100139

label: Mixed sequencing platforms: only WGS samples can show rearrangements
text: PITFALL: Studies often combine WGS and exome samples; exome/array data cannot detect intergenic or balanced rearrangement junctions, so pooling them dilutes any rearrangement-based statistic. CHECK: Read data_gene_panel_matrix.txt (mutations/cna/structural_variants columns) and EXOME_SEQUENCED_IN_BARBIERI_ET_AL_2012 in the sample table to see which samples have WGS-based SV calls. IF FOUND: Restrict rearrangement analyses to samples profiled for structural variants by WGS and report the denominator. SOURCE: https://docs.cbioportal.org/file-formats/

label: compound claim, no CNA table
text: PITFALL: The hypothesis is compound (KIT mutations AND focal amplifications), but the data folder has no copy-number/GISTIC/segment table; ABSOLUTE_EXTRACT_PLOIDY is whole-genome ploidy, not focal amplification, and must not be used as a proxy. label: use provided subtype column
text: PITFALL: Re-deriving subtypes from the MAF can disagree with the study's own assignment (subtypes use BRAF/RAS hotspots and any NF1 mutation, applied hierarchically BRAF>RAS>NF1). CHECK: data_clinical_sample.txt MUTATION_TYPE has BRAF_Hotspot_Mutants=150, RAS_Hotspot_Mutants=92, NF1_Any_Mutants=28, Triple_WT=46, NA=43; use it as the grouping and exclude NA rather than calling NA wild-type. label: KIT driver vs passenger (TMB)

CHECK: tabulate KIT mutations by Variant_Classification and protein change per subtype; separately count known hotspot/oncogenic KIT (exon 11/13/17, e.g. L576P, K642E, V559, W557, D816, N822, V560) vs other; compare TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS by subtype. IF FOUND: base the main test on oncogenic/hotspot KIT (and nonsynonymous excluding silent), and present any-KIT as sensitivity; optionally adjust for TMB (logistic regression with log TMB). SOURCE: https://journals.lww.com/melanomaresearch/abstract/2015/02000/driver_kit_mutations_in_melanoma_cluster_in_four.12.aspx

label: exclude silent/noncoding KIT

CHECK: value counts of Variant_Classification for Hugo_Symbol==KIT. IF FOUND: restrict to protein-altering classes (Missense, Nonsense, Frame_Shift, In_Frame, Splice_Site) before computing per-sample KIT status. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3989533/

IF FOUND: dedupe to one sample per patient (or keep the subtype-labelled one) and report n per group. SOURCE: https://gdc.cancer.gov/about-data/publications/skcm_2015

label: Purity confounds VAF shifts
text: PITFALL: Mouse stroma in xenografts and human stroma in patient tumours change tumour purity, so raw VAFs shift between tumour (T) and xenograft (X) samples even when clonal make-up is unchanged; a uniform VAF rise in X looks like 'selection'. CHECK: Estimate purity per sample (e.g., median VAF of clonal/truncal mutations x2, or from CN segment amplitudes) and test whether VAF changes are a global scale shift or mutation-specific (some up, some down, some lost). IF FOUND: Convert VAF to cancer cell fraction (CCF = VAF*CN/(purity*multiplicity)) or normalise to truncal mutations before claiming selection; selection = divergent CCF changes among mutations, not a uniform shift. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7026725/ ; https://perspectivesinmedicine.cshlp.org/content/7/8/a026625.full

label: Copy number confounds VAF
text: PITFALL: VAF depends on local copy number and LOH; a CN gain/loss arising in the xenograft changes VAF without any change in the fraction of cells carrying the mutation. CHECK: For each mutation compared between T and X, look up the segment mean (data_cna_hg19.seg / data_log2_cna.txt) in both samples; flag mutations in segments whose CN differs between T and X. IF FOUND: Restrict the VAF/CCF comparison to CN-stable regions or adjust for CN; note that new/lost CN segments in X are themselves evidence of clonal change and can be analysed directly. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7867630/

label: Binomial noise vs real change
text: PITFALL: Treating any VAF difference or presence/absence between T and X as clonal selection ignores binomial read-sampling noise, which is large at WGS depth (~30-60x). CHECK: Use t_ref_count/t_alt_count to run per-mutation tests (Fisher exact/binomial or beta-binomial) between T and X, and count mutations with significant change in both directions, with multiple-testing correction. IF FOUND: Only call selection from mutations whose CCF change is statistically significant (e.g., subclonal in T at CCF<0.3 rising to clonal in X, or clonal clusters lost), and report how many patients show it. SOURCE: https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pcbi.1004416

label: Platform/depth mismatch
text: PITFALL: The data contain both whole-genome (~30-60x) and deep targeted sequencing samples; mutations 'absent' in a WGS sample may simply be below its detection limit, and mixing platforms when comparing T vs X manufactures gains/losses. CHECK: Compare T and X within the same sequencing type (targeted vs targeted, WGS vs WGS); for each 'lost' mutation check read depth at that site in the other sample. IF FOUND: Prefer the deep targeted data (same panel sites across T and X passages) for VAF trajectories; treat absence at low depth as unknown, not lost. SOURCE: https://doi.org/10.1186/s13073-020-00791-w

label: Mouse-read artefacts
text: PITFALL: Mouse reads mismapped to human create false variants that appear only in xenografts (and can look like newly emerged clones), and also dilute VAFs. CHECK: Look for X-only mutations with low VAF, recurrent across unrelated patients' xenografts, or clustered in genes/positions with high mouse homology; check whether they are recurrent across patients. IF FOUND: Exclude recurrent cross-patient X-only variants and low-VAF X-only calls; base selection claims on changes in prevalence of mutations already present in T rather than X-only novel calls. SOURCE: https://doi.org/10.1186/s12920-019-0551-2 ; https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13059-019-1849-2

label: Unmatched normal: germline
text: PITFALL: The clinical table marks samples SOMATIC_STATUS=Unmatched; residual germline heterozygous SNPs (VAF~0.5 everywhere, ~1 under LOH) are stable across T and X and dilute any signal, or shift with LOH and mimic selection. CHECK: Flag variants with VAF~0.5 in all samples of a patient, non-coding/silent variants, and dbSNP-annotated sites; see whether Matched_Norm_Sample_Barcode is populated. IF FOUND: Remove likely germline variants before quantifying clonal shifts; interpret VAF jumps from 0.5 to 1 as LOH events, not clonal expansion. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4561496/

label: Spatial sampling vs selection
text: PITFALL: The patient tumour (T) sample is one bulk piece and the xenograft is grown from a different fragment, so a clone that dominates X may already be dominant in that fragment; spatial sampling bias can mimic selection, and single-sample bulk data can give an 'illusion of clonality'. CHECK: Where a patient has multiple independent xenograft lines (suffixes A,B,C,D at the same passage, e.g. SA532X1A-D) test whether the same clones expand reproducibly across lines and how much of the change happens at T->X1 versus later passages. IF FOUND: Reproducible expansion of the same low-prevalence T clone across replicate engraftments or clear loss of many T subclonal mutations at X1 supports selection at initial engraftment; inconsistent shifts suggest drift/sampling - state this limitation in the reasoning. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7867630/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4841575/

label: Engraftment vs later passage; primary vs metastatic
text: PITFALL: The hypothesis is specifically about INITIAL engraftment (T -> first passage X0/X1) and about BOTH primary and metastatic tumours; using only late-passage samples, or patients without a T sample (e.g., SA429, SA496 have only X samples), tests passage drift, not engraftment. CHECK: Parse SAMPLE_ID (T = patient tumour, X<n>[letter] = passage n, replicate letter), keep patients with both T and X0/X1 samples, and look for any annotation of primary vs metastatic origin (the clinical sample table may lack it). IF FOUND: Base the verdict on T->X1 comparisons; if primary/metastatic status is not encoded, say so and judge whether selection is seen across the patient set regardless (do not default to Not verifiable if T and X1 mutation/CN data exist). SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5659952/

label: Low heterogeneity tumours show no selection
text: PITFALL: Clonal selection can only be detected in tumours that are polyclonal at baseline; averaging over all patients can hide strong selection in a subset (in published PDX series, skewed engraftment was seen in roughly half of models), or a few noisy patients can be over-interpreted. CHECK: Per patient, estimate how many subclonal (low-CCF) mutations T has and summarise outcome patient by patient (stable / expansion / loss). IF FOUND: Report the number of patients with clear selection; the hypothesis ('clonal selection occurs') is supported if a substantial number of patients show reproducible clonal shifts, not that every patient must. SOURCE: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-022-29304-6 ; https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-019-14106-0

label: Unit of analysis: paired pre/post
text: PITFALL: Comparing ERBB2 amplification rates between all PRE-TX and all POST-TX samples (unpaired, different patients) confounds treatment selection with case mix; acquired-resistance loss of ERBB2 is a within-patient event. CHECK: In data_clinical_sample.txt count patients with >1 sample (about 34 patients) and, among HER2+ trastuzumab-treated patients, those with both a PRE-TX and a POST-TX sample (IMPACT_PRE_POST); also check the YJ-her-* samples present only in data_cna.txt and the seg file, which look like multi-region/paired research samples (e.g. -P1/-P2/-M1a). IF FOUND: Base the main test on within-patient pre to post ERBB2 transitions (AMP to non-AMP), report counts per patient, and treat unpaired cohort rates as secondary only. SOURCE: https://doi.org/10.1002/ijc.30408

label: Define acquired vs primary resistance
text: PITFALL: Acquired trastuzumab resistance means progression after initial benefit; mixing in primary non-responders (HER2_RESPONSE POD, short time on first line) or untreated patients dilutes or fakes the association. CHECK: Restrict to patients treated with trastuzumab (patient TREATMENT/DETAILS_FIRST_LINE_COMMENTS mention tras; HER2_RESPONSE not NA) and tabulate HER2_RESPONSE (CR/PR/SD vs POD) and HER2_TTP_ON_1ST_LINE_MONTHS for the post-progression samples. IF FOUND: Analyse acquired (initial CR/PR/SD then progression, post-treatment biopsy) separately from primary resistance; state which group any ERBB2-loss cases fall in. SOURCE: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41389-023-00466-2

label: NGS ERBB2 false negatives: purity
text: PITFALL: Panel-NGS ERBB2 amplification calls (discrete CNA = 2 / HER2_IMPACT AMP) become false negatives when tumour purity is low or the amplification is heterogeneous, so an apparent post-treatment 'loss' may be technical rather than clonal selection. CHECK: For each pre-AMP to post-non-AMP case, look at the ERBB2-region log2 seg.mean in data_cna_hg19.seg (chr17 ~39.69-39.73 Mb hg19) and HER2_IMPACT_LR, and check whether other clonal events (e.g. TP53 mutation VAF in data_mutations.txt, other amplicons) are still present at normal levels in the post sample. IF FOUND: Count a case as true subclonal loss only if ERBB2 log ratio falls while other truncal alterations keep their signal; flag low-purity cases as indeterminate rather than as loss. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5397722/

label: Discrete CNA thresholds
text: PITFALL: In cBioPortal discrete CNA, 2 = high-level amplification and 1 = low-level gain; treating a 2 to 1 change as loss, or binarising only on 2, can misclassify partial loss of amplification. CHECK: Tabulate ERBB2 discrete values (data_cna.txt) alongside the continuous seg.mean and HER2_IMPACT_LR for each paired sample. IF FOUND: Use the continuous log ratio as the primary measure of decline, use 2 vs not-2 only as a sensitivity analysis, and report both. SOURCE: https://docs.cbioportal.org/user-guide/faq/

label: Spatial heterogeneity/site confound
text: PITFALL: HER2 status differs between primary tumour and metastases (and between regions) even without treatment, so a pre=primary vs post=metastasis comparison can show ERBB2 loss through site discordance rather than treatment selection. CHECK: For each pair compare SAMPLE_TYPE and SITE_OF_TISSUE_BIOPSY, and check untreated multi-sample patients (or multi-region YJ-her samples taken before treatment) for baseline ERBB2 discordance. IF FOUND: Compare the rate of AMP loss in treated pairs against baseline spatial discordance; same-site pairs give stronger evidence; mention heterogeneous ERBB2 at baseline as evidence of a pre-existing non-amplified subclone. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3267049/

label: Clonal selection evidence
text: PITFALL: Calling ERBB2 loss 'selection of a subclone' needs evidence of shared ancestry (same tumour) plus loss of the amplicon, not just a negative call. CHECK: In paired samples verify shared truncal mutations (same TP53 etc. in data_mutations.txt) and look for a pre-treatment sample or region that already lacks ERBB2 amplification (heterogeneity), consistent with an outgrowing subclone. IF FOUND: Report cases as clonal selection only when ancestry is shared and the non-amplified population is detectable before or after treatment; otherwise label them as ERBB2 loss of uncertain mechanism. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5027494/

label: Small-n inference
text: PITFALL: With only a handful of paired trastuzumab-progression cases, a non-significant test does not show that there is no association, and a p-value is not the right tool for a case-series finding. CHECK: Count the informative pairs and discordant pairs (AMP to non-AMP vs non-AMP to AMP); if comparing paired binary status use exact/mid-p McNemar; compare the loss frequency in post-trastuzumab pairs with a reference group (untreated or non-progressing pairs). IF FOUND: Report counts and proportions with exact confidence intervals; recurrent ERBB2 loss in post-progression samples that is not seen in controls is evidence of an association even without p<0.05; do not turn 'not significant' into 'no association'. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3716987/

label: Other resistance mechanisms
text: PITFALL: In paired data, post-progression samples may also gain RTK/RAS/PI3K alterations (EGFR/MET/KRAS/PIK3CA amp or mutation, CCNE1) or ERBB2 exon16 deletion; ignoring them can wrongly attribute or deny the role of ERBB2 loss. CHECK: For each post-progression sample list new alterations versus its pre sample in data_cna.txt, data_mutations.txt and data_sv.txt (ERBB2 SVs). IF FOUND: Report ERBB2 loss as one of several mechanisms (counts per mechanism); its co-occurrence with other mechanisms does not cancel the association. SOURCE: https://aacrjournals.org/cancerdiscovery/article/9/2/199/10771/EGFR-and-MET-Amplifications-Determine-Response-to

CHECK: Cross-check sample IDs across data_cna.txt, the seg file, data_gene_panel_matrix.txt and data_clinical_sample.txt; confirm ERBB2 and comparator genes are covered for each sample. IF FOUND: Map extra sample IDs to patients by their naming pattern (e.g. YJ-her-005-P1/P2), keep them in the paired analysis, and treat uncovered genes as NA. SOURCE: https://github.com/cBioPortal/cbioportal/blob/master/docs/File-Formats.md

label: Coding filter hides promoter variants
text: PITFALL: Filtering the MAF to coding/nonsynonymous Variant_Classification values (as maftools, TMB and many cBioPortal-style pipelines do) silently removes promoter variants, which are labelled 5'Flank, 5'UTR or IGR (VEP Consequence upstream_gene_variant / 5_prime_UTR_variant), so promoter mutations look absent. CHECK: tabulate Variant_Classification and Consequence for every NFKBIE row with no class filter. IF FOUND: count 5'Flank/upstream/5'UTR rows as candidate promoter mutations; never apply a coding-only filter for a promoter hypothesis. SOURCE: https://docs.gdc.cancer.gov/Encyclopedia/pages/Mutation_Annotation_Format_TCGAv2/ ; https://github.com/genome-nexus/annotation-tools/blob/master/vcf2maf.py

label: Search promoter by coordinates not symbol
text: PITFALL: vcf2maf assigns each variant to one transcript only, so a promoter variant near NFKBIE can be listed under a neighbouring gene's Hugo_Symbol or as IGR/Unknown, and a Hugo_Symbol search misses it. CHECK: besides Hugo_Symbol==NFKBIE, search by coordinates (take NFKBIE gene span from the file's own NFKBIE rows/Gene/Transcript columns, GRCh37 chr6 ~44.2 Mb) plus a few kb on the upstream side, and grep all annotation columns (e.g. all-effects/Consequence) for NFKBIE. IF FOUND: include those rows as NFKBIE promoter candidates. SOURCE: https://github.com/mskcc/vcf2maf/

label: Strand defines promoter side
text: PITFALL: NFKBIE lies on the minus strand, so its promoter/5' upstream region is at HIGHER genomic coordinates than the gene's coding start; looking below the gene start finds the 3' flank instead. CHECK: confirm strand from transcript annotation in the MAF (e.g. STRAND/Transcript columns, 5'Flank vs 3'Flank labels) and define the promoter window relative to the TSS on the correct side. IF FOUND: use the 5'Flank label/upstream side consistent with the strand. SOURCE: https://useast.ensembl.org/info/genome/variation/prediction/predicted_data.html

label: Coverage caveat for promoter absence
text: PITFALL: Absence of promoter calls can reflect lack of coverage (exome capture targets exons; GC-rich promoters are poorly covered) rather than true absence. CHECK: check whether the MAF contains any non-coding classes (5'Flank, IGR, Intron) at all and how many samples have WGS (GENE_PANEL says Exome, Whole Genome); look at t_ref_count/t_alt_count of any promoter calls. IF FOUND: if the MAF has no noncoding calls at all, absence is uninformative (lean Not verifiable); if noncoding calls exist and NFKBIE promoter calls are seen in desmoplastic samples, that directly contradicts 'absent'. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13136893/ ; https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371%2Fjournal.pone.0204912

label: Absent claim: one event refutes
text: PITFALL: A claim that a mutation is 'absent' is refuted by even one credible somatic event; conversely zero events in n samples only bounds prevalence at about 3/n (rule of three), not proves absence. CHECK: count distinct desmoplastic samples carrying an NFKBIE promoter variant (unique Tumor_Sample_Barcode, deduplicate repeated rows/positions) and note recurrent positions. IF FOUND: >=1 credible somatic promoter mutation in a DESM sample contradicts the hypothesis (False); do not demand statistical significance. SOURCE: https://doi.org/10.1080/00031305.1997.10473947

label: Cohort definition Pure vs Mixed
text: PITFALL: Restricting the cohort wrongly, e.g. dropping 'Mixed' DETAILED_SAMPLE_HISTOLOGY_CATEGORY samples or failing to match Tumor_Sample_Barcode to SAMPLE_ID, changes which desmoplastic tumours are counted. CHECK: confirm ONCOTREE_CODE/CANCER_TYPE_DETAILED for all samples (both Pure and Mixed are desmoplastic melanoma) and that every MAF barcode joins to the sample table. label: CNA metric choice
text: PITFALL: 'number of copy number alterations' can be operationalised as raw segment count, count of segments with |seg.mean| above a threshold, or fraction of genome altered (FGA, length-weighted), and these can rank samples differently. CHECK: for each sample in data_cna_hg19.seg compute (a) total segments, (b) segments with |seg.mean|>0.2 (and >0.1, >0.3), (c) FGA = altered bp / total bp, and see whether the JuP3-JP vs JuP3-DCIS vs JuP3-IDC ordering agrees across all of them. IF FOUND (disagreement): report all metrics, base the call on thresholded altered-segment count/FGA rather than raw segments, and only call True/False if the direction is consistent. SOURCE: https://www.biostars.org/p/406584/ ; https://search.r-project.org/CRAN/refmans/CINmetrics/html/fga.html

label: Threshold sensitivity
text: PITFALL: cBioPortal-style FGA uses |log2|>0.2 in some docs and >0.1 in others; a borderline threshold can flip which lesion has more CNAs when segment means are small (WES seg means are often ~±0.05-0.3). CHECK: plot/list the distribution of seg.mean per sample and recompute counts at 0.1, 0.2, 0.3. IF FOUND (ranking flips): treat the result as threshold-dependent, prefer the conventional 0.2 but state the instability; do not claim a large difference. SOURCE: https://groups.google.com/g/cbioportal/c/SqtGhn-AZ4s ; https://openbiox.github.io/Bizard/Omics/FgaPlot.html

label: Purity dilution
text: PITFALL: lower tumour purity (stromal/normal contamination, common in small in-situ or papillary lesions) shrinks log2 ratios toward 0, so a fixed threshold undercalls CNAs in that sample and makes it look less altered. CHECK: compare the spread of seg.mean (e.g. SD or max |seg.mean|) and the VAF distribution of mutations (t_alt_count/(t_alt_count+t_ref_count) in data_mutations.txt) between JuP3-JP, -DCIS, -IDC; a sample with much lower median VAF is likely lower purity. IF FOUND: interpret a lower thresholded count in the low-purity sample cautiously; check whether the segment breakpoints (count of segments) still show the same ranking. SOURCE: https://cnvkit.readthedocs.io/en/latest/calling.html ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9881684/

label: Matched trio n=1
text: PITFALL: 'associated DCIS and IDC-NST' means lesions from the same patient; in this data only patient JuP3 has JP, DCIS and IDC (JuP1, JuP2 are JP-only), so the comparison is a single matched trio with no statistical power and pooling JuP1/JuP2 JP samples against JuP3 DCIS/IDC would confound patient with lesion type. CHECK: parse PATIENT_ID/SAMPLE_ID from data_clinical_sample.txt and confirm which samples share a patient. IF FOUND: make the primary comparison within JuP3 (JP vs DCIS vs IDC) descriptively; use JuP1/JuP2 only as context (e.g. are JP samples generally low/high CNA), not as a pooled group test. SOURCE: https://genomemedicine.biomedcentral.com/articles/10.1186/s13073-017-0442-0

label: Spurious small segments
text: PITFALL: segmentation noise produces short segments with few markers and adjacent segments with near-identical means, inflating raw segment counts in noisier samples (count reflects data quality, not biology). CHECK: count segments with small num.mark (e.g. <10-20) per sample and count of segments that remain after merging adjacent segments with |delta seg.mean|<0.1; compare across samples. IF FOUND: count only altered segments above threshold and with adequate num.mark, or use length-weighted FGA. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5062840/ ; https://rdrr.io/bioc/DNAcopy/man/segment.html

label: Baseline centering
text: PITFALL: log2 profiles are median-centred, so in a highly aneuploid/genome-doubled sample the baseline shifts and gains/losses get mis-signed or missed, distorting CNA counts between samples. CHECK: per sample, compute length-weighted median seg.mean and whether a large share of the genome sits at a common offset from 0. IF FOUND: re-centre on the dominant state or report counts relative to the sample's own baseline, and compare total |deviation| rather than signed gain/loss counts. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9294200/ ; https://www.biostars.org/p/257680/

label: Not-verifiable trap
text: PITFALL: analysts may label CNA claims Not verifiable or use the TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS column (a mutation measure) as a CNA proxy. CHECK: data_cna_hg19.seg contains segment-level log2 copy ratios for all 5 samples including JuP3-JP, JuP3-DCIS, JuP3-IDC, so CNA burden is directly measurable. IF FOUND: compute CNA burden from the seg file, do not substitute TMB; choose True/False based on the within-JuP3 comparison. SOURCE: https://www.biostars.org/p/406584/

label: Sex chromosomes
text: PITFALL: chromosome X/Y segments vary with sex and reference choice and are usually excluded from FGA/CNA counts; including them can add spurious alterations. CHECK: list unique chrom values in the seg file per sample and whether X/23/Y segments differ. IF FOUND: compute burden on autosomes only (and report with/without). SOURCE: https://search.r-project.org/CRAN/refmans/CINmetrics/html/fga.html

reason: Whether a paired WES reference exists decides whether the hypothesis can be tested at all, so the teams must establish data provenance before picking a label.
text: Testing whether targeted-panel TMB correlates with whole-exome (WES) TMB needs both measurements on the same tumours. Before any analysis, search every clinical column header and description line, the gene panel matrix, and the mutation file (e.g. sequencing-assay or centre fields) for any WES/WXS/exome assay or a second TMB value from another platform, and count how many samples have both. Use only values present in the given tables; do not bring in published or literature TMB values as data.

reason: This prevents a false 'correlation' result produced by comparing a panel-derived quantity with itself.
text: Columns such as TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS and MUTATION_RATE in the sample table, and mutation counts recomputed from data_mutations.txt, can all come from the same targeted-panel calls. Correlating them with each other is circular and says nothing about agreement with WES. Confirm where each TMB-like column comes from (using its description line and the panel matrix) before treating any of them as an exome reference.

reason: The choice of statistic can flip the conclusion when the data are skewed. This sets how a correlation hypothesis should be tested.
text: If paired panel and WES TMB values exist, make rank or log-scale correlation the primary test: Spearman on raw values and Pearson on log(TMB+1). A raw Pearson r can be driven by a few ultra-high-TMB outliers, so rerun the test without the top outliers. Report agreement (Bland-Altman bias and limits, slope against the identity line) separately, because the hypothesis is about correlation, not agreement.

reason: Mixing panel versions without normalising adds artificial noise or bias to any TMB comparison.
text: Samples may have been sequenced on different MSK-IMPACT panel versions with different territories (about 0.897, 1.016 and 1.139 Mb for IMPACT341, 410 and 468). Raw mutation counts are not comparable across versions. Tabulate the panel per sample, normalise counts per Mb using the panel-specific size or adjust for panel version, and only then compare with anything else.

text: The hypothesis concerns how engrafted rectal-cancer tumoroids respond to chemotherapy in mice. Before any analysis, list every column of data_clinical_sample.txt and data_clinical_patient.txt (and check the other files) for a variable that directly measures that response: xenograft/engraftment status, treatment vs control arm, tumour-volume measurements over time, T/C ratio, tumour growth inhibition, AUC, or response/sensitivity categories per model. If such a variable exists, compute response per model and judge the spread between models, not pooled means. Report what you found either way.

text: Do not substitute proxies for murine chemotherapy response. THERAPY_PRIOR_TO_DERIVATION records the patient's treatment exposure before the tumoroid was made, not how the engrafted tumoroid responded in mice. Likewise, genomic differences between tumoroids (mutations, CNAs, TMB, MSI, primary vs metastasis, tumour-vs-tumoroid concordance) do not by themselves show differing drug sensitivity; genotype is not a response phenotype.

reason: This keeps the team from confusing 'no data' with 'evidence against' when choosing between labels.
text: Not finding a difference, or not finding a relevant variable, is absence of evidence. It does not show that response is uniform, and it does not show that response varies. A contradicting conclusion requires a directly measured relevant variable whose analysis goes against the claim.

label: Oncogenic filtering without OncoKB column
text: PITFALL: The mutation file has no OncoKB/oncogenic annotation column, so counting every non-silent variant as an 'oncogenic alteration' adds VUS and passenger mutations. This matters most for large tumour-suppressor genes such as RNF43 and SMAD4 and for PIK3CA non-hotspots. CHECK: look for ONCOKB/oncogenic columns (only Annotation_Status exists). Then list the HGVSp_Short spectrum per gene. IF FOUND: approximate OncoKB rules. KRAS: hotspots at codons 12, 13, 59, 61, 117 and 146. BRAF: V600E plus class 2/3 hotspots. PIK3CA: hotspot codons such as E542, E545, H1047 and the known oncogenic list. AKT1: E17K. RNF43 and SMAD4: truncating variants (nonsense, frameshift, splice) plus known hotspots, e.g. SMAD4 R361. Run a sensitivity analysis comparing 'all non-silent' with 'putative driver'. SOURCE: https://faq.oncokb.org/technical
