label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q1 (optimism): PROGNOSTIC_MODEL was likely derived on this 1001-patient cohort, so its apparent AIC (2082 vs 2124) and 5-yr AUC (0.706 vs 0.698) edges over IPI are inflated and the inputs cannot be rebuilt to correct them. IPI is fixed externally and has no optimism. The paired C-index is the right head-to-head test, and it does not favour the genetic model: 0.673 vs 0.682 for IPI 0-5 in 618 patients, and 0.660 (n=753) vs 0.683 (n=754) in all available patients. Changes method: yes.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q2 (extra metrics): 60-month truncated C was 0.671 for the genetic model vs 0.683 for IPI 0-5 (paired bootstrap diff -0.011, 95% CI -0.059 to 0.039). Nested LR tests: adding the genetic model to IPI gives chi2 85, adding IPI to the genetic model gives chi2 51, so each adds to the other. KM 5-yr OS by genetic group: 93/68/49%; by IPI 3-group: 84/64/45%. Being independently prognostic is not outperformance. The wider KM spread and the LR asymmetry are in-sample and subject to optimism.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q3 (other established markers): cell of origin has no column in the data. BCL2, MYC and BCL6 FISH are each missing in 876/1001 patients (MYC positive in only 14), so IPI is the only established comparator that can be tested. Any claim about 'current established methods' therefore reduces to genetic model vs IPI.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY to ERG_FISH question: ERG_FISH_RESULT has 12 'Translocation with deletion' and 11 'Translocation' (59 NA); all 23 are ERG-fusion positive in data_sv. Seg mean copy number in hg19 chr21 40.1-42.8 Mb (between ERG and TMPRSS2) has median -0.52 in the deletion group (11/12 below -0.2) and median 0.015 in the translocation group (0/11 below -0.2), so the flag is internally consistent. It records a deletion-linked fusion mechanism at a single locus, not a chain across loci, so it does not test chromoplexy and does not change the Not verifiable label.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY to sample-overlap question: of 82 clinical samples, 57 are WGS-profiled for mutations and SVs, 57 have seg data, and 56 have gene-level CNA. The 25 samples with no SAMPLE_TYPE have no seg, SV or FISH data. The analysable set is 57 WGS tumours, all with matching clinical rows. This does not add any rearrangement-junction variable and does not change the Not verifiable label.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY to deep-deletion/seg-breakpoint question: 22 of 57 WGS tumours have deep deletions (GISTIC -2) at PTEN, RB1, TP53, CHD1, NKX3-1, CDKN1B, BRCA2, FOXP1, TP63 or MAP3K7. Seg breakpoints (|delta seg.mean|>0.3) occur on a median of 20 chromosomes in both deep-deleted and other tumours (median 220 vs 164 breakpoints; Mann-Whitney p=0.32), and 96% of tumours have breakpoints on at least 5 chromosomes. Co-occurrence across chromosomes is therefore near-universal background and cannot separate interdependent from independent events without junction partners, so there is no usable proxy and the label stays Not verifiable.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY to library findings: the ChainFinder finding (breakpoint junctions with partner and orientation are required, and copy number alone cannot link breaks across chromosomes) matches the data. data_sv.txt has only gene-level Site1/Site2 symbols with no coordinates, and the seg-based check showed breakpoints spread across all chromosomes in nearly every tumour. The Edel/Esplit finding matches the seg check, where 11/12 Edel tumours show the interstitial 21q22 loss. Neither finding gives a chain-level test.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY to director Q on CN breakpoints: across 57 seg samples, fusion-positive (n=28, data_sv) and fusion-negative (n=29) samples do not differ in segment breakpoint count (median 192 vs 181, MWU p=0.91), focal deletions <20Mb (p=0.89), chromosomes carrying focal deletions (p=0.41), or deep deletions at PTEN/NKX3-1/CHD1/RB1/TP53/CDKN1B/FOXP1/BRCA2 (p=0.81). PTEN losses are mostly focal (14/20 <10Mb), NKX3-1 mostly arm-level (median 21Mb). CN segments cannot join breakpoints across chromosomes or see balanced joins, so they cannot test interdependence; this is now a tested result, not an assumption. Does not change label (Not verifiable).

label: REPLY
text: REPLY to director Q on ERG_FISH_RESULT: of 12 'Translocation with deletion' samples, 11 show chr21 loss (weighted seg.mean < -0.2 over 40.1-42.8Mb hg19) vs 0 of 11 'Translocation' samples; mean -0.56 vs +0.01. The column is valid, but it records a single-locus interstitial deletion that produces TMPRSS2-ERG, not a chain of rearrangements across chromosomes. So it is not a variable for chromoplexy interdependence and does not change the Not verifiable label.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY to director Q on two-part hypothesis: part (a), identifying interdependent translocations and deletions, needs breakpoint coordinates, partners and orientation. The relevant columns are data_sv.txt (gene-only fusion list, no coordinates), ERG_FISH_RESULT/ETS_FUSION_SEQ (single fusion per sample) and seg (CN only). None links breakpoints into chains. Part (b), chromoplexy accounting for gene dysregulation: dysregulation is visible (ERG fusions in 28/57 samples, deep deletions at PTEN in 7, NKX3-1 in 7, CHD1 in 5, no expression data), but no column assigns these to a chromoplexy event. No variable points for or against either part, so Not verifiable stands.

text: REPLY to the FILTER/ExAC question: none of the 11 nonsynonymous ERBB-PI3K pathway variants carry FILTER=common_variant. The 68 common_variant rows are elsewhere. Only TSC1 R22W has ExAC_AF (1.7e-5). Excluding common variants leaves 9/56 hit samples, so this check does not change the method.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY to the length-matched null question: under a SLAPenrich-style per-sample Poisson null (per-sample nonsynonymous rate times summed pathway CDS length, exome 30-35 Mb, common variants excluded), the 45-gene list gives 9 observed against 4.4-5.1 expected (p=0.02-0.05). The earlier p=0.005 came from a null that ignored gene length. The enrichment is much weaker than reported.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY to the pathway-definition question: with a fixed standard list (TCGA PanCanAtlas PI3K 29 genes plus EGFR/ERBB2-4), NPC has 6/56 altered samples against 3.1-3.6 expected (p=0.07-0.13, not significant). TCGA PI3K alone gives 4/56 against 2.6-2.9 expected (p=0.25-0.34). The 14-gene core gives 5/56, p=0.03-0.05. The label changes from False to True.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY to the hotspot/functional question: the Hotspot column is 0 for all 1575 rows. Of the pathway hits, only PIK3CA E545K is a known canonical hotspot, in 1/56 samples. ERBB2 I767M and ERBB3 E919K/K329R are SIFT-deleterious and PolyPhen-probably-damaging, but MA:FImpact is low or neutral for them. The others (PIK3CG, MTOR A1778S, NRG1, PIK3R6) are tolerated or benign. The earlier conclusion rested on the enrichment test, and that test does not hold on the standard list.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY (IPI coding): On the n=618/185-event complete set, the genomic PROGNOSTIC_MODEL has lower AIC than every IPI coding (G 2082 vs IPI 0-5 linear 2119, categorical 2124, 4-group 2126, 0-1/2-3/4-5 3-group 2124-2125, R-IPI 0/1-2/3-5 2137), but Harrell C is at parity: G 0.673 vs IPI 0-5 0.682, 4-group 0.672, 3-group 0.664, R-IPI 0.646; bootstrap C(G)-C(IPI) CIs all include 0 (-0.010 [-0.063,0.037] for 0-5; +0.028 [-0.024,0.075] for R-IPI). Reference is IPI 0-5 / standard 4 groups. Conclusion unchanged under each coding for discrimination; AIC favours G under all codings but is in-sample.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY (criterion / absence vs evidence): 'Outperform' implies a clearly better head-to-head discrimination against IPI, judged out-of-sample or optimism-corrected. A mutation-only 3-group Cox model built on this cohort had apparent C 0.609 but 5-fold CV C 0.511, showing large in-sample optimism here, so PROGNOSTIC_MODEL's in-sample AIC edge over the fixed IPI is not valid evidence of superiority. Its discrimination equals, not beats, IPI (point estimate -0.010 vs IPI 0-5), which I treat as evidence against the claimed superiority rather than mere absence; label stays False with moderate confidence.

text: REPLY Q1 (broad MSS cohort): the 302 added samples with missing MSI_STATUS were kept only if MSI_SCORE<3 (MSIsensor MSS cut-off); none has MOLECULAR_SUBTYPE MSI and their TMB max is 16.6 (MSI samples median 53), so they are MSS; 2 MSI_STATUS=MSS samples with MOLECULAR_SUBTYPE MSI are now also excluded. Broad cohort stays primary, strict reported as sensitivity.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q2 (Early Stage Primary): the earlier cohort did include 45 (strict) / 55 (broad) Early Stage Primary samples. Restricting to mCRC Primary/Metastasis: broad n=239R/661L, PIK3CA 20.5% vs 12.6% p=0.004, AKT1 2.5% vs 0.3% p=0.006, SMAD4 18.8% vs 12.0% p=0.011; strict n=160R/457L, PIK3CA 17.5 vs 12.3% p=0.11, AKT1 1.2 vs 0% p=0.07, SMAD4 17.5 vs 11.8% p=0.08. Same direction, no label change.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q3 (criterion): no formal pre-set criterion was written earlier; the criterion applied was right>left in all six genes with significance in the main (broad) cohort. In metastasis-only samples (strict n=74R/228L) KRAS, BRAF, SMAD4 are significant, PIK3CA (18.9 vs 10.5%) and RNF43 (4.1 vs 0.9%) trend right, AKT1 is 0/74 vs 0/228, so all-six enrichment does not hold in that underpowered subset; no gene goes left>right.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q4 (panels): all six genes have mutations called on IMPACT341, 410 and 468 samples in data_mutations, consistent with the library finding that they are core genes on all three panels. Panel mix differs slightly by side (IMPACT341 27% of right vs 18% of left in broad mCRC), but excluding IMPACT341 samples leaves all six right>left with p<0.035 in the broad cohort.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY library findings: excluding RNF43 G659fs (OncoKB inconclusive) changed no MSS RNF43 counts (G659fs calls lie in MSI tumours), and expanding the curated SMAD4 missense list added 2-3 SMAD4 cases per side; MSI_SCORE<3 is the MSS convention used. Label stays True.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY (primary test): The prespecified primary test was the 22-gene curated ERBB-PI3K list across all 56 samples. It gives O/E 1.72, Poisson p=0.14 (sample-level p=0.19), or p=0.12 after common_variant filtering. That is not significant at alpha 0.05, and the best subset variant (p~0.02) fails Bonferroni over ~6 variants. So the label was revised from False to True.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY (duplicates): data_mutations.txt has 1575 rows and 0 duplicates by sample+chromosome+position. 315 rows have CANONICAL not YES (308 have PICK missing), but these are distinct variants, not transcript duplicates. All 6 ERBB-PI3K hits are CANONICAL=YES, PICK=1. Deduplicating changes nothing.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY (common_variant): 68 of 1550 non-synonymous rows have FILTER=common_variant, and none of the 6 ERBB-PI3K hits do. The only hit with any ExAC frequency is TSC1 R22W (ExAC_AF 1.7e-5). Dropping flagged rows from the background raises O/E from 1.72 to 1.80 and lowers p from 0.14 to 0.12; the result is still not significant.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY (criterion): bd31-team-a's criterion was: all six genes higher on the right, most of them individually significant after FDR, and the pooled any-of-six test significant. It was not 'all six individually significant'. Under the strict all-six-significant rule, SMAD4 fails with the driver definition (13.4% vs 10.2%, q=0.20) but passes when all non-silent variants are counted. Answer kept as True; SMAD4 is the stated weak point.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY (SV): data_sv.txt has 8 SVs in the six genes (2 BRAF fusions, 1 BRAF in-frame deletion, 3 RNF43, 2 SMAD4). Adding all of them to the driver calls changes BRAF to 14.2% vs 5.2% and RNF43 to 6.3% vs 1.3%, still significant. SMAD4 stays at q=0.20 and every direction is unchanged. Method unchanged.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY (MCRC_TYPE): Restricting to mCRC Primary or mCRC Metastasis (884 patients) leaves the driver results almost the same: PIK3CA 19.7% vs 12.5% (q=0.011), AKT1 2.9% vs 0.3% (q=0.003), SMAD4 13.4% vs 10.5% (q=0.23), and any-of-six OR 5.8. With non-silent variants every gene is significant, including SMAD4 at q=0.005. Directions are unchanged, so the method and label stay.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY (MOLECULAR_SUBTYPE): Excluding MOLECULAR_SUBTYPE POLE or MSI removes 7 more patients (934 remain) and changes nothing material: 5 of 6 genes have q<0.01, SMAD4 has q=0.34, and any-of-six OR is 5.55. The label stays True.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY (panel library finding): All six genes are on IMPACT341, 410 and 468, so every sample is a valid denominator. The panel-by-side crosstab is Left 138/636/5 and Right 75/262/4 for 341/410/468. Coverage cannot bias these counts, and no change is needed. The MSI cutoffs from the library (MSS <3, MSI-H >=10) match the cohort definition already in use.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q1 (replicate first passages): the seg file and log2 file contain exactly one xenograft CN profile per patient (e.g. SA501X1A only, no X1B), so convergence/divergence of independent engraftments cannot be tested; this removes a strong comparator but does not change the method.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q1 (missing mutation rows): 12 of 42 samples have no mutation rows; all have TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS=0 and normal coverage (537-906x), 9 are FP. Earlier code treated them as zero. Treating them as missing (dropping pairs with either sample missing) leaves FN 8 vs FP 4 patients, new-mutation median 1.5 vs 0.5 (mean 1.75 vs 0.5); FN>FP holds either way, so the method does not change.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q2 (primary vs metastatic): no origin variable exists in the clinical table; the data can test selection at engraftment of breast tumours pooled (13 T/X pairs) but cannot show it separately for primary and metastatic tumours. I treat this as a limit on scope, not a reason for Not verifiable, and lowered confidence.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q2 (SNV/indel only, leave-one-out): New SNVs/indels only, per patient: FN median 1.5 mean 1.7 (union over later samples) vs FP median 0.5 mean 0.7, MWU p=0.15 (not significant alone). Dropping each of the 20 patients in turn, FN mean exceeded FP mean in all 20 versions; total (mutations+CNA) also never reversed. Direction holds; method unchanged, but mutation-only evidence is weak in significance.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q3 (X0/X1 pairs vs passage drift): fraction of 1Mb bins with |residual|>0.3 after centring+slope fit, with chromosome bootstrap 95% CI: SA536 0.055, SA493 0.077, SA531 0.107, SA533 0.096, SA501 0.013, SA534 0.153, SA535 0.073. Drift references: SA501 X1A->X5A 0.058 [0.023-0.107], SA429 X2A->X5A 0.253. 0/7 exceed SA429 drift; 5/7 point estimates exceed SA501 drift but CIs overlap. SA501 T->X1A (0.013) shows the pipeline can reproduce a profile, so the 5-15% changes in other pairs are above that floor. Evidence of T->X1 change being greater than later drift is weak.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q3 (no common mutations): Within-patient reading: 6 of 10 FN patients share 1-6 mutations between earlier and later samples (e.g. P-0074869 shares 6 incl TP53 R248Q), so FN tumours keep common mutations. Across-patient reading: only TP53 is newly acquired in 2+ FN patients (P-0073133 E258*, early sample 60% purity, solid; P-0051132 C176F, early sample 10% purity with no mutation rows, uncertain). Genes mutated at any time in 2+ FN patients: TP53 (4), BCOR (2), CTNNB1 (2). Reading (b) evidence against is thus weak; label rests mainly on the 'fewer' part, which is contradicted.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q4 (unmatched T vs matched X calling): among WGS T/first-X pairs, T-only calls (n=364) have a variant-class mix similar to shared calls (n=2220) (e.g. intron 16% vs 18%, missense 25% vs 30%), none carry dbSNP IDs, and only 1.9% recur across patients (shared 0%), so germline residue does not dominate the T-only set. But in SA501, 4 of 8 T-only variants (absent at X1A) come back at X5A, meaning they are detection-sensitivity losses, not real losses. X-only calls are enriched for Silent (39% vs 10% shared), which points to artifacts. Mutation presence/absence is weak evidence; CN is the main evidence.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q4 (CNA sub-threshold/purity): Segment-level check of later-sample segments with |seg.mean|>=0.8 against earlier-sample seg.mean over the same interval: 24 of 47 FN and 10 of 12 FP high-level segments had earlier same-sign log-ratio >=30% of the later value (likely pre-existing, sub-threshold or purity effects; e.g. all of P-0074869, P-0060318). Clearly new segments (earlier ratio <0.3) remain in 7 of 10 FN patients (23 segments) vs 2 of 10 FP patients (2 segments). Excluding sub-threshold changes keeps FN>FP; method unchanged.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY (replicate lines): No patient has two sibling xenograft lines at the same passage with WGS/CN data; the only multi-X patients are SA501 (X1A, X5A) and SA429 (X2A, X5A), which are the same lineage at different passages, so a test of whether independent lines reproduce the same shift is impossible. The conclusion does not change, but this stays a stated limitation.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q1 (missed calls): In bd40 there are no UNCALLED rows (all 78 mutation rows SOMATIC), so earlier-sample VAF at a 'new' position cannot be looked up. Flagging new events as plausible misses (earlier-sample purity <=30% or unknown, or expected earlier VAF <5%) flags all events in P-0013120 (base purity 30), P-0051132 (base purity 10), P-0050430 (base 30) and FP P-0069477 (purity unknown). The seg.mean check is mixed: in P-0013120 the baseline CDH1 segment is -0.54 (a loss that was probably missed), but MDM2 is -0.04 against a later 3.04 (a real gain). In P-0048073 the baseline PPM1D segment is 0.80 against a later 0.98, a missed call. After removal, FN per-patient new alterations are still >= FP (median 2.0 vs 1.0, mean 4.7 vs 1.2), but p=0.37, so the FN>FP difference is no longer significant. The direction never reverses.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q2 (split by type, baseline swap): With the primary sample as baseline, FN vs FP per-patient max new events: SNV/indel only median 1.5 vs 0 (p=0.052), CNA only 4.0 vs 0 (p=0.029), SV only 0 vs 0. Using the lowest T-suffix as baseline changes 6 patients (4 FP, 2 FN) and gives all 4.0 vs 1.0 (p=0.008), mutations 1.5 vs 0.5 (p=0.17), CNA 3.0 vs 0 (p=0.007). FN>=FP holds in every version, and the method is unchanged; most of the FN excess comes from CNAs.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY (origin): Across all clinical columns (PATIENT_ID, SAMPLE_ID, SEQUENCING_TYPE, SAMPLE_CLASS, ONCOTREE_CODE=BRCA, CANCER_TYPE, CANCER_TYPE_DETAILED, SOMATIC_STATUS, TMB) and the MAF columns, nothing encodes primary vs metastatic site. So that part of the claim cannot be tested separately. The core claim (selection at T->X0/X1) is still testable, so the label does not change to Not verifiable.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY (library findings): data_mutations.txt Mutation_Status is SOMATIC for all 78 rows, with no UNCALLED rows to drop. The purity finding was checked through the seg.mean comparison (see the Q4 reply). Purity artefacts explain many apparent new CNAs, but FN>FP holds after excluding them.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q3 (empty mutation samples): The 12 samples with no mutation rows (9 FP, 3 FN) all have TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS=0, so the original analysis treated them as zero mutations. If pairs with an empty-mutation sample are dropped as missing, the per-patient median new alterations is FN 4.0 (n=8) vs FP 1.5 (n=4). The direction does not change.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY (later-passage null): Later passages of the same lineage, both called Matched, show discordance as large as or larger than T->X1. SA501 X1A->X5A lost 24% of mutations (35/146), and the CN residual |d|>0.5 is 2.8% vs 0.1% for T->X1A. SA429 X2A->X5A lost 13.6%, CN r=0.79. T->X0/X1 lost 6.5-16%, CN r=0.87-0.99. Engraftment discordance therefore does not clearly exceed the multi-passage baseline, so selection specific to engraftment is not proven; per passage the change is similar. Of the 124 SA501 T mutations, 108 persist to X5A, which shows gradual clonal drift. The label stays True with lower confidence.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q4 (TP53 and shared mutations): TP53 is mutated in 4 FN-RMS patients. It was present at baseline and kept in 2 (P-0050430 R248Q, P-0074869 R248Q). It was new in the later sample in 2: P-0073133 E258*, with baseline purity 60% and baseline TP53-wild-type, robust; and P-0051132 C176F, with baseline purity 10%, likely a missed call. Earlier-later shared mutations per FN patient: P-0013120 0, P-0018770 1, P-0035844 0, P-0048073 0, P-0050430 1, P-0051132 0, P-0051453 1, P-0073133 2, P-0074869 6, P-0077663 3. Acquired events recurrent across FN patients are TP53 mutations (2), MDM2 amplification (2) and BAP1 deletion (2). So 'no common mutations' is contradicted under either reading (recurrent genes or shared truncal mutations), though with small numbers.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY on the library findings: The library's UNCALLED check was run; bd40 data_mutations has no UNCALLED rows, so nothing needs dropping. The purity-artifact caution for +/-2 CNAs is borne out in part: several 'new' CNAs sit opposite low-purity baselines (P-0013120 30%, P-0051132 10%), and seg.mean shows sub-threshold signal at some genes (CDH1, PPM1D). Removing them keeps FN>=FP in direction but loses significance. The label stays False, with lower confidence.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY (Unmatched T calls): The dbSNP_RS column is empty for every WGS call, so no population-database check is possible. T-only calls (n=216 across 7 early pairs) are all SNPs. Their Silent fraction is 12% vs 10% for shared calls, and 2.3% recur in another patient vs 0% for shared. So T-only calls do not look grossly like germline residue, though without VAF that cannot be excluded. X-only calls are the suspicious set: 46% Silent vs 10% for shared, consistent with mouse-read artefacts. Selection claims should therefore rest on T mutations lost in X, not on X gains. This does not change the method.
